input.command: find src -type f; cat package.json; grep -rn "remoteUrl\|cloneRepo\|register" src
input.description: List src files and search for remoteUrl usage

input.command: cat -n src/routes.ts; cat -n src/config.ts; cat -n src/api.ts
input.description: Show routes, config and api files
Show store file and search for URL validation

input.reason: I read src/git-auth.ts, src/worktree.ts, src/routes.ts, src/config.ts and src/store.ts. At src/git-auth.ts:8, gitAuthArgs decides whether to add the token with `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`. That is a substring test on the whole URL, not a check of the parsed host, so it passes for URLs like `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git`. When it passes, the function returns `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`. cloneRepo at src/worktree.ts:15 calls it with SERVICE_TOKEN (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN, from src/config.ts:4) and clones the same URL. registerRepo at src/routes.ts:19-22 takes remoteUrl from the request body. It only checks that the value is non-empty, then passes it to store.insertRepo and cloneRepo. store.insertRepo does not validate it. I found no URL parsing, host allow-list or tests anywhere in src that would stop this.
input.summary: Substring host check leaks GitHub service token to lookalike remote hosts

findings.text: The host check is a substring match, so a remote URL such as `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and receives the service token in an `Authorization` header. Any user who can register a repository can collect the token.
findings.reason: Each claim holds. (1) Substring match: src/git-auth.ts:8 is `if (remoteUrl.includes("github.com"))`, a substring test on the whole URL that never parses the host. (2) The example URL passes: `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` contains "github.com", and line 9 then returns `["-c", `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`]`, which makes git send an Authorization header to the remote. (3) The token is the service token: cloneRepo at src/worktree.ts:15 passes SERVICE_TOKEN, which src/config.ts:4 sets to process.env.HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN. (4) Any registering user can collect it: registerRepo at src/routes.ts:19-22 reads remoteUrl from req.body, only checks that it is non-empty, and calls cloneRepo with it. store.insertRepo at src/store.ts:17 stores the URL without validating it.

findings.text: `cloneRepo` passes the user-supplied `remoteUrl` straight to `gitAuthArgs` with the service token, so `git clone` sends the token to whatever host the URL names, as long as the URL contains the substring `github.com` anywhere.
findings.reason: Each claim holds. (1) The URL is user-supplied and passed straight through: src/routes.ts:19 takes remoteUrl from req.body, line 22 calls cloneRepo({ id, remoteUrl, ... }), and src/worktree.ts:15 calls gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN) with no validation in between. (2) git clone sends the token to that host: the same line runs exec("git", [...authArgs, "clone", repo.remoteUrl, dest]), so the http.extraHeader Authorization header goes with requests to the host in the URL. (3) The URL only needs to contain github.com somewhere: src/git-auth.ts:8 uses remoteUrl.includes("github.com"), which matches the substring anywhere in the URL, including the path.

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable credential leak. Any authenticated user can call registerRepo with a URL that contains "github.com" but points at a host they control. cloneRepo then sends the service's GitHub bearer token (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) to that host in the Authorization header. That exposes whatever the service token can access.
